item.title: Dark homes, dry taps, idle factories: Gurgaon hit by 16-hour power cuts amid strike
item.description: Thousands of households in Gurgaon faced power and water outages due to a strike by electricity department employees. The disruption affected industrial units, causing significant production delays and potential financial losses. Many residents struggled with basic needs as inverters failed and water supply ceased. The strike was in response to a decision to grant a private electricity distribution license.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: ‘Disgrace at so many levels’: Tharoor on removal of Raihan Vadra’s exhibition photos
item.dc:creator: ABHISHEK MISHRA

item.title: 'I don’t play this game to prove anyone wrong': Samson after India's 1st T20I win
item.description: Sanju Samson says he focuses on his game and trusts his process rather than trying to silence critics. His comments came after India chased 230 against New Zealand to record their highest-ever successful T20I run chase. Samson scored 67 off 33 balls, while Naman Dhir's unbeaten 42 off 15 deliveries sealed India's four-wicket win and a 1-0 series lead.
item.dc:creator: JYOTIRMOY HALDER

item.title: Amazon abandons data centres plan it paid $427 mn for; donates $5 mn for housing
item.description: Amazon has decided not to proceed with its plans for developing four data centres in Virginia. The company will instead donate roughly 25 acres of the site to Loudoun County for community facilities. This agreement includes a contribution of $5 million towards the county's affordable housing initiatives. The decision comes after feedback from local leaders and the community regarding the proposed data centres.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Hawaii police dog finds missing 70-year-old hiker, second rescue in 2 months
item.description: After missing for over a day in Hawaii Volcanoes National Park, 70-year-old David Arai was successfully located by Trina, a skilled police dog, who led the search team through dense foliage. Found two miles from his rental car and suffering from dehydration, Arai expressed immense gratitude to his rescuers and is now contemplating adopting Trina, who has proven her tracking abilities with two recent rescues.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: On UP voter list: 'Ram Ne Yadav Ko Mara, s/o Murkh Chandra Yadav'
item.description: Electoral rolls in Uttar Pradesh have reported unusual entries that have sparked concerns over their accuracy. Notable entries include voters with odd names and details that do not align with reality. The Chief Electoral Officer stated that fewer than 150 inaccuracies were identified among 14.8 lakh registered voters. Despite the digital system's introduction, verification processes remain questioned after complaints from various political parties.
item.dc:creator: ARVIND CHAUHAN

item.title: Ishan ruled out of 2nd T20I, paves way for Sooryavanshi's return to playing XI
item.description: Ishan Kishan has been ruled out of the second T20I against New Zealand due to a low-grade injury. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, a promising teenager, could make his return to the playing XI. India secured a record-breaking chase in the first T20I, leading the series 1-0. The BCCI medical team is monitoring Kishan's recovery while discussing potential replacements. The upcoming match is set to take place at Hagley Oval in Christchurch.
item.dc:creator: NITESH DUBEY

item.title: 1890 Sherlock Holmes first edition found in charity donations sold for £11,520
item.description: During his life, Gregor Mendel's essential studies on plant hybridization remained largely unappreciated. His landmark paper, titled 'Experiments on Plant Hybrids', was released in 1866, and in a remarkable turn, a rare edition sold for $640,000 in 2026. Mendel's discoveries on genetic inheritance laid the groundwork for contemporary biology, serving as a potent reminder of the delayed acknowledgment often faced by revolutionary scientific contributions.
item.dc:creator: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK

item.title: Haldhar Nag left school after Class 3, later won Padma Shri for his poetry
item.description: Haldhar Nag, a gifted poet from Odisha, faced profound challenges after his father's death, leading him to leave school. Despite this setback, his poignant poetry in the Kosli language gained national recognition, inspiring academic studies that underscore its cultural importance. Nag's inaugural poem was published in 1990, reflecting on social themes. In 2016, he was awarded the Padma Shri, marking his vital role in promoting regional literature in scholarly discussions.
item.dc:creator: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK

item.title: After renaming Lake Ontario, Google CEO rejects US request to rename Atlantic Ocean
item.description: President Trump has recently proposed renaming the Atlantic Ocean, following prior discussions about the Atlantic Ocean. During a recent event, he mentioned contacting Google Maps regarding these renaming efforts. Google CEO Sundar Pichai reportedly declined his proposal on the grounds that oceans encompass multiple countries. This follows the US administration's earlier renaming of Lake Ontario to Lake America for US users.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Portland man spent $48,412 on backyard; rentals brought in $85,000 by 2025
item.description: Rob Nachbar skillfully turned his once-simple backyard in Portland into a thriving rental space known as Pong Springs. This five-year renovation, which cost $48,412, prioritized weather-resistant structures and enhanced privacy features. Since its launch on Swimply, Nachbar has generated approximately $106,000 in revenue. The yard not only hosts various events but also provides the family with a serene private retreat—combining leisure and financial success.
item.dc:creator: TOI REAL ESTATE DESK

item.title: China’s 'eyes in the sky' multiply, India’s surveillance fleet faces a numbers game
item.description: Recent satellite imagery indicates that four KJ-3000 Airborne Early Warning aircraft are located at Xi'an Aircraft Company. This suggests that serial production of the aircraft may soon commence, enhancing China's AEW&C capabilities. The KJ-3000 is based on the Y-20B transport aircraft, aiming to address existing limitations in China’s AEW&C fleet. In comparison, India's airborne early warning capability remains limited with fewer aircraft currently in service.
item.dc:creator: DHRUV YADAV

item.title: Govt plans colour-coded DLs for Indians, foreigners; may scrap affidavits
item.description: Life insurance policies, too, would no longer be accepted as proof. Proposing sweeping changes to the driving licence (DL) regime under Motor Vehicles Rules, the road transport ministry Wednesday issued a draft notification to raise the pass mark for the online safe-driving tutorial assessment from the current 60% to 75%.
item.dc:creator: DIPAK K DASH

item.title: India's WTC Final chances: What South Africa's win over Australia means
item.description: South Africa’s innings win over Australia has tightened the World Test Championship final race. Australia remain top, while India sit fifth with seven Tests left against New Zealand and Australia. India need 62 points to reach a 60 PCT and cannot lose more than two matches. They also need at least two of Australia, New Zealand and South Africa to drop points.
item.dc:creator: JYOTIRMOY HALDER

item.title: ‘Ridiculed for eating beef’ at school, 16-year-old Tamil Nadu boy dies by suicide
item.description: In Coimbatore, a tragic incident unfolded as 16-year-old A Akilan, a Scheduled Caste student, took his own life allegedly due to persistent harassment from peers and a teacher over his dietary preferences. His mother highlighted that repeated pleas to school officials were ignored, resulting in this heartbreaking event. Authorities have initiated a case against the teacher, headmaster, and two students, inciting public protests for justice and a thorough investigation.
item.dc:creator: TYSION PRABHU

item.title: 3 Sri Lankans, Tamil Nadu woman detained near Indo-Nepal border
item.description: On Wednesday night, Sashastra Seema Bal apprehended a group of four individuals near the India-Nepal border in Bahraich district. Among them were three Sri Lankan nationals and a woman from Tamil Nadu attempting to cross into Nepal through a forest route. Security personnel discovered that the passports of the Sri Lankans had expired three months earlier. Authorities are currently investigating their travel circumstances and intended destination.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Texas farmer went from 27 sheep to overseeing 10,000 across 40,000 acres
item.description: JR Howard experienced hardships early on with only a small number of sheep, making it tough to earn a living. However, after landing a grazing contract with solar farms, he expanded his flock and income significantly. This eco-friendly grazing method is being embraced by renewable energy companies as a cost-effective way to manage vegetation, while farmers benefit from expansive grazing land without hefty property expenses.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Can Kimi Antonelli clinch the F1 2026 title in Austin?
item.description: Kimi Antonelli heads to the United States Grand Prix in Austin with a 102-point lead in the 2026 Formula 1 championship. With six races remaining, the Mercedes youngster could move closer to becoming the youngest world champion in F1 history. George Russell, Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen remain mathematically in contention, but Antonelli's title hopes could receive a decisive boost if results go his way in Texas.
item.dc:creator: NITESH DUBEY

item.title: 'Lifting sanctions will make Putin stronger': Zelenskyy differs with Trump on Russia
item.dc:creator: ABHISHEK MISHRA

item.title: California family spent $4,000 turning its front yard into Jurassic Park
item.description: In Granada Hills, a family has dedicated $4,000 to create an elaborate Jurassic Park-themed display for Halloween. After investing over 200 hours, they've constructed life-sized dinosaur replicas and an automated escape show, complete with grand entrance gates. Open to the public at no cost, this attraction fosters community spirit as neighbors flock to capture the experience and enjoy this festive installation.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Jason Momoa buys Sam Neill's former 4.92-hectare NZ estate for NZ$15m
item.description: Jason Momoa has recently acquired a significant property in Queenstown, New Zealand for NZ$15 million. The estate, formerly owned by Sir Sam Neill, demonstrates the increasing interest in the local real estate market. Property values in the region have risen significantly, attracting overseas buyers. Momoa has deep connections to New Zealand, having visited frequently for leisure and work. He has also invested in the local film industry and nightlife scene.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Virginia teen's model improves simulated earthquake sensor coverage by 16.7%
item.description: A 14-year-old student from Williamsburg, Virginia, has become one of 30 finalists in a national science competition after developing a mathematical model to improve earthquake sensor placement. Isabel Rossi's six-month research project showed that adding just five sensors could increase simulated detection coverage by 16.7%. She used earthquake records from California and mathematical methods to identify better sensor locations.
item.dc:creator: TOI SCIENCE DESK

item.title: Will decide on any notice to remove CEC according to rules: LS Speaker Om Birla
item.description: Both the Lok Sabha Speaker and the Rajya Sabha chairman had rejected previous notices from the opposition, saying their allegations “do not prima facie meet the high constitutional bar for removal proceedings”. Birla noted the process for removal of the chief election commissioner was the same as for removing a Supreme Court judge.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: PHP security flaws trigger global scramble; CERT-In flags vulnerabilities
item.description: Google Cloud executives Chris Betz, chief information security officer, and Raluca Ada Popa, head of Gemini Security at Google DeepMind, said PHP and cybersecurity firm Wiz Research disclosed the two vulnerabilities after research that used multiple AI models to identify and help remediate them. Google Cloud said its own infrastructure was not vulnerable, but warned that customers running PHP applications on the platform could be exposed
item.dc:creator: SHILPA PHADNIS

item.title: Hospitals ‘overcharging’ is a malpractice: Govt to Supreme Court
item.description: In an affidavit filed in SC on the issue of capping prices of all medicines and medical consumables, chemicals and fertilisers ministry said that patients have a very low bargaining position with respect to hospitals, resulting in various malpractices. The affidavit noted the irony of India being home to companies making cheap drugs but patients here having to pay way above the manufacturing price, as well as patients being subjected to overcharging by hospitals.
item.dc:creator: AMIT ANAND CHOUDHARY

item.title: Amid attacks, sales surge at Kolkata Left bookstalls
item.description: Book stalls set up by Left parties saw significant sales increases during Durga Puja amid incidents of vandalism. The CPM stall at Jadavpur 8B bus stand recorded sales of Rs 16 lakh, nearly four times last year's figures. Despite attacks, sales for other Left stalls also increased, evidencing a broader engagement with literature. Politicians from various parties expressed solidarity with the Left stalls amidst ongoing disputes.
item.dc:creator: DIPAWALI MITRA AND POULAMI ROY

item.title: Anahat scripts history, storms into maiden PSA Gold semi-final
item.description: Anahat Singh pulled off an impressive comeback against Salma Hany, clinching her spot in the semi-finals at a PSA Gold-level event after a nail-biting five-game match that lasted 42 minutes. The 18-year-old, facing a 1-2 deficit, demonstrated resilience and skill. Anahat will now go head-to-head with Malaysia's Sivasangari Subramaniam, reigniting their rivalry from the Asian Games final, solidifying her remarkable tournament journey in Redwood City.
item.dc:creator: NITESH DUBEY

item.title: Centre betrayed us, now want full statehood for Ladakh: Sonam Wangchuk
item.description: Wangchuk said the representatives of Leh Apex Body (LAB) and Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA) had come prepared for Oct 22 talks in Delhi as a follow up of the May 15 meeting in Leh, with the expectation that the MHA and Ladakh bodies' respective drafts on contours and powers of UT-level body and district councils, would be discussed.
item.dc:creator: BHARTI JAIN AND NASEER GANAI

item.title: Will back all meaningful efforts for Ukraine peace, PM Modi assures Poland's Tusk
item.description: PM Modi and his Polish counterpart Tusk expressed deepest concern in a joint statement over the war in Ukraine, including its tragic humanitarian consequences and the impact on Global South. In his media statement, Modi assured Tusk that whether it is Ukraine or West Asia, India will continue to support every meaningful effort for peace.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Congress defaming India to shield Nehru-Gandhi family: PM Modi
item.description: “Dimagi naxals have captured Congress so much that it has lost its ability to think. Those who used to cause destruction in forests are now determined to wreak havoc on the country through Congress,” PM Modi said, referring to hardcore Left elements accused of being sympathetic to Maoists and now vocal in protests against EC and govt.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Tom Brady donated $170,000 Salem State speaking fee to charities in 2015
item.description: Tom Brady collected $170,000 for a speaking gig at Salem State University, generously donating the entire sum to charity. He allocated $50,000 to Best Buddies and distributed the remaining funds to various other organizations. With approximately 4,000 attendees present, ticket sales effectively covered his speaking fee. However, the event was notable for Brady facing questions about the NFL's Deflategate saga. The university reported a financial profit from hosting the event.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK
